name: Didjits
label: Touch and Go
lede: Two brothers from Mattoon, Illinois, a bassist who rode motorcycles, a frontman in sunglasses and a feather boa, and a song the Offspring took to eleven million homes.

eras.title: Little Richard in a Mattoon basement
eras.text: The Didjits started as a teenage band in Mattoon, a railroad town in central Illinois, and got good once Rick Sims stopped trying to please anyone. The plan, as he tells it, was to be a modern Little Richard and Jerry Lee Lewis, played at punk speed.

q: I wasn't making music that I liked, music for myself.
years.h: Rick and Brad Sims start the Didjits in Mattoon, Illinois
years.p: Rick Sims on guitar and vocals, his brother Brad Sims on drums. Rick later said this first version was music for other people, not himself.
years.xp: Between Didjits line-ups, Rick Sims sang and played drums in UXB, with [[Doug Evans|17c6a990-b88b-4ed1-a11e-5d880c0a8c4b]] on guitar and Mike Rankin on bass. When the Didjits came back, Sims returned to guitar and Evans moved to bass. UXB's tapes finally came out in 2024 on the bonus LP Bring Me the Head of Jaco Pastorius.

years.h: Fizzjob: a whole album in one 12-hour day
years.p: The Didjits cut their debut with producer [[Iain Burgess|1572ff4f-9714-4d7e-804a-49b86a74a855]] at Chicago Recording Company in a single 12-hour session and put it out themselves on Bam Bam.

eras.title: Thanksgiving at Corey Rusk's
eras.text: A tape handed over at a holiday dinner got the Didjits onto Touch and Go, where they made their best-known records with Iain Burgess and a pseudonymous Steve Albini. One of those songs would travel much farther than the band did.

years.h: Steve Albini's cassette gets Didjits signed to Touch and Go
years.p: Steve Albini brought a tape of Hey Judester to Corey Rusk's Thanksgiving dinner. Rusk and his wife Lisa, who'd written the Didjits off as a novelty act, decided to release it.
years.xp:
Albini engineered several Didjits records under the pseudonym Reggie Stiggs. Hey Judester itself was produced by Iain Burgess and the band, and runs 26 minutes, with a cover of Little Richard's Lucille.

The press split. The Chicago Sun-Times called it the band's high point. The Toronto Star heard a pile of racial and sexist slurs, while granting the songs were meant as parody. On one Bay Area stop, Rick Sims says, [[Jello Biafra|2280ca0e-6968-4349-8c36-cb0cbd6ee95f]] asked to record the set and the band's own sound man wouldn't allow it.

years.p: The Didjits' second Touch and Go album includes Killboy Powerhead, the song that four years later lands on an album that sells in the millions.

years.h: Full Nelson Reilly, the original trio's last album
years.p: Rick Sims, Doug Evans and Brad Sims make their third Touch and Go album together.

years.h: Brad Sims quits the Didjits to raise a family
years.p: After Full Nelson Reilly, drummer Brad Sims leaves his brother's band to raise a family. The Didjits keep going with borrowed drummers.

eras.title: Drummers from Texas, and a bottle to the head
eras.text: With Brad gone the Didjits drafted Rey Washam of Scratch Acid and Rapeman, then Todd Cole. The end came messily in Chicago: a bassist who didn't turn up and a stage skit the crowd hated.

years.h: Little Miss Carriage! with Rey Washam on drums
years.p: [[Rey Washam|33b09380-db28-4c9c-9fdd-ab5c20049c61]], who had drummed for [[Big Boys|fde1cff2-5a7b-4e8c-9666-110fa90500fb]], [[Scratch Acid|75687111-1585-4df2-83e6-ce52e7fa2bb0]] and [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]]'s [[Rapeman|899dea17-b403-42e0-9673-2623c40081af]], sits in on the Didjits' 1992 EP.

years.h: Que Sirhan Sirhan, the Didjits' last album
years.p: Todd Cole on drums, [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]] engineering, a [[Plasmatics|3fec8b00-4142-4129-96f5-1c9bf65e8e8f]] cover (Monkey Suit) and Judge Hot Fudge, whose video airs on Beavis and Butt-Head. The band also turns up on MTV's 120 Minutes.

years.big: One bottle and a very quiet room
years.h: The Didjits' last show ends with a breakaway bottle
years.p: Doug Evans no-showed a Chicago gig, and [[Pierre Kezdy|061ef98c-497e-4a61-9464-10bf622c3c24]] of [[Pegboy|13e78eec-9ee4-47f2-a50e-2a9f519cb6e2]] filled in on bass. At the final show, Rick Sims hit actor Joey Slotnick with a breakaway bottle in a skit, and the crowd turned on them.
years.xp:
Bandcamp Daily's history marks the skit as the end of the band. The Didjits didn't play again for twelve years.

The following year he joined the [[Supersuckers|6fa09822-bbe4-4ff8-901d-4a39a4dd82e9]], replacing guitarist Ron Heathman and playing on The Sacrilicious Sounds of the Supersuckers, produced by [[Paul Leary|976549ea-72bb-45ea-9431-3f07b4ed7dc8]] of the [[Butthole Surfers|2339bc21-aa92-4850-86f0-4bb9433910c8]].

years.p: Chris Bagarozzi of Claw Hammer played the Didjits tape during the Offspring's sessions, and Killboy Powerhead made the album. Bandcamp Daily puts Smash at 11 million-plus sold; Rick Sims says 14 million.

eras.title: Gaza Strippers, Fred Schneider, and a goodbye
eras.text: Rick Sims kept playing loud in other people's bands and his own, from the Supersuckers to Gaza Strippers. The original three got back together once, for Touch and Go's birthday. Doug Evans moved to California and never stopped playing.

years.p: Sims forms Gaza Strippers with Darren Hooper and Todd Marino; three albums follow through 2002 on Lookout! and Man's Ruin. He also backs [[Fred Schneider|43bcca8b-9edc-4997-8343-122350e790bf]] of the B-52's in Deadly Cupcake, on the Albini-produced Just... Fred.

years.h: The original Didjits reunite for Touch and Go's 25th
years.p: Rick Sims, Doug Evans and Brad Sims play Touch and Go's 25th anniversary block party in Chicago, then a Champaign show the following weekend.

years.h: Didjits bassist Doug Evans dies in California at 53
years.p: Evans had been playing in Blöwer with his partner Merilee Kuchon. Rick Sims called him one of the most generous people he knew; plans for another reunion were shelved.
years.xp: The AV Club's obituary did not give a cause of death. Friends said he was happiest on his motorcycle, still playing music, and Corey Rusk remembered his skill and patience.

eras.title: Strictly dynamite
eras.text: Touch and Go boxed up the Didjits' best, UXB tapes and all, and Rick Sims put a new rhythm section together for the band's first shows in almost two decades.

years.p: The Didjits' best-of comes with a bonus LP, Bring Me the Head of Jaco Pastorius, collecting Rick Sims's pre-Didjits band UXB.

yt: Didjits live at Riot Fest, Sept 19, 2025
years.h: Didjits play Riot Fest with a new rhythm section
years.p: Rick Sims returns with Billy Fury, singer of Soy City Stranglers, on bass and Beanz, his cousin's son, on drums. They also play Chicago's Empty Bottle.
